title: Plán legislativních prací 2026 — 21 transposition tasks flagged for EU infringement exposure
money_note: No sanction amount is published; Article 260(3) TFEU lump-sum and penalty payments are set by the Court, not by the plan
summary: The government legislative plan for the rest of 2026, annex 1 to resolution 175 of 23 March 2026, carries footnotes on 21 of its legislative tasks warning of EU infringement proceedings; on five the transposition deadline has already been missed and on one, the capital-market act transposing directive 2022/2381, proceedings have already been opened with a real prospect of a financial sanction under Article 260(3) TFEU. The affected files include the AI act adaptation, the Data Act bill, the Cyber Resilience Act bill, the energy act hydrogen rules, the critical raw materials act, the construction-products act, the labour code, the beneficial-owners register, the waste act, the packaging act and the air protection act.
notes: Checklist source 2 (Plán legislativních prací vlády 2026). Counted mechanically from the resort sections of the plan PDF (pdftotext -layout): 21 superscript footnote markers on task rows, of which 16 read 'Predlozeni navrhu v danem terminu je spojeno s hrozbou zahajeni rizeni' and 5 read 'Implementacni lhuta u predpisu EU nebyla dodrzena' — one of those five (PV-1, capital-market act, directive 2022/2381 gender balance on boards, implementation due 12.24) says proceedings were already opened. Tasks and their planned effective dates: PV-1 07.26, PV-2 07.26, MPO-1 AI act 07.26, MPO-2 Data Act 07.26, MPO-5 energy-performance 08.26, MPO-6 construction products 08.26, MPO-7 CRA 09.26, MPO-8 energy act 09.26, MPO-9 critical raw materials 09.26, MPO-12 07.27, MD-1 vehicle operation 11.26, MD-2 civil aviation 12.26, MPSV-3 labour code 01.27, MSp-1 beneficial owners 07.26, MV-1 criminal procedure 11.26, MZd-1 public health 12.26, MZP-1 waste 09.26, MZP-2 IED 09.26, MZP-3 air protection 12.26, MZP-5 packaging 11.26, MZP-8 end-of-life products 06.27. Dates: plan adopted 2026-03-23 (usneseni 175); submission months run 03.2026-12.2026; effective dates 07.2026-01.2029. Market: transposition-gap advisory and the compliance waves that land late and fast. Fifteen records in the corpus already cite this same plan PDF for individual bills; this record is the plan-level infringement count, not one of them.
quote: Implementační lhůta u předpisu EU nebyla dodržena a bylo zahájeno řízení pro nesplnění povinností plynoucích z práva Evropské unie proti České republice s reálnou možností navržení finanční sankce podle čl. 260 odst. 3 SFEU.

title: Vodní zákon novela — extended producer responsibility for pharma and cosmetics funds quaternary treatment
money_note: RIA: total investment in quaternary treatment estimated at about 120bn CZK, converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR; it is the sector total the EPR scheme is designed to fund, not a single contract. Commission impact assessment cited at about 1.2bn EUR/year EU-wide
summary: The Ministry of Environment and Ministry of Agriculture draft amending Act 254/2001 transposes directive 2024/3019 and builds a Czech extended-producer-responsibility scheme in which makers of human medicines and cosmetics fund the quaternary treatment stage that removes micropollutants, with an authorised collective system, tonnage reporting and fee flows. The RIA puts total quaternary-treatment investment at about 120bn CZK if left to public budgets, expects an average consumer price rise of about 0.6 percent, and proposes an effective date of June 2027.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions), read for the draft the scripted veklep feed surfaced as veklep-KORNDXBH65S3 in data/signals/regulation/2026-09-02.jsonl. The scan does not re-mint that id; this is the state-authored problem definition, its dates and its costs, from the Zaverecna zprava RIA attachment. The RIA is a joint document for two acts: 254/2001 (vodni zakon, effective 06/2027, this record) and 274/2001 (vodovody a kanalizace, effective 07/2027, two further records). RIA variants under evaluation: one collective PRO versus several competing PROs (varianta 5c), with MZP authorising and supervising either way, plus registration of individual systems and a health-surveillance system for urban wastewater at MZd. Directive permits up to 20 percent public co-funding. Dates: material authorised 2026-08-27, in comment procedure; effective 06/2027; directive transposition deadline 31 July 2027. Distinct from reg-uwwtd-epr, which records the EU directive itself: this is the Czech bill, its national cost estimate and its PRO design choice. Market: PRO set-up and operation, tonnage reporting for pharma and cosmetics, micropollutant-removal technology at named plants.
quote: Nejvýrazněji bude podnikatelské prostředí zasaženo v části týkající se rozšířené odpovědnosti výrobce, která se vztahuje na výrobce humánních léčivých přípravků a kosmetických přípravků.

title: Zákon o vodovodech a kanalizacích — four-yearly energy assessment for 200-plus wastewater plants
money_note: RIA estimates 8-15bn CZK of investment to reach energy neutrality in the sector; the lower bound of the state's own range converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR is used and the upper bound is 612m EUR. Operating costs put at hundreds of millions CZK a year
summary: The Ministry of Agriculture draft amending Act 274/2001 makes owners of urban wastewater treatment plants commission an energy assessment of the plant and its sewer network every four years, approve its results and report prescribed data, as directive 2024/3019 requires on the path to energy neutrality. The RIA says the duty falls on more than 200 plants at 10000 population equivalent and above, puts sector investment at 8 to 15bn CZK, and proposes an effective date of July 2027.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions) for the draft surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDXBH65S3; the veklep id is not re-minted. RIA states the current act contains no duty to produce an energy assessment at the scope and interval the directive requires, and that economically justified costs of the assessment and of the measures it recommends may be passed into the stocne (sewerage charge) calculation, so the cost reaches connected customers indirectly. Dates: material authorised 2026-08-27, comment procedure open; RIA summary sheet gives effective 07/2027 and implementation deadline 07/2027. Kraje separately owe an update of their plany rozvoje vodovodu a kanalizaci: RIA prices seven observed past update contracts at 0.428m to 37.8m CZK, median 2.9m CZK. Market: energy-audit and process-optimisation services for WWTP operators, biogas and heat recovery retrofits, reporting tooling; buyers are municipalities and regional water companies.
quote: Tato povinnost by se měla vztahovat na více než 200 čistíren městských odpadních vod s látkovým zatížením odpovídajícím 10 000 ekvivalentních obyvatel a vyšším.

title: Srážkové vody — Czech draft scraps every exemption from the stormwater sewerage charge
money_note: RIA quantifies annual impact at almost 5bn CZK on municipal budgets, almost 0.5bn CZK on regions, under 30m CZK on the transport ministry for motorways and class I roads and under 27m CZK for the rail operators; about 5.5bn CZK a year converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR
summary: The draft amending Act 274/2001 deletes section 20 paragraph 6, which today exempts motorways, roads, local and public-access service roads, national and regional rail land, zoos, cemeteries and residential buildings and households from paying for stormwater discharged into public sewers. The RIA quantifies the new annual bill at almost 5bn CZK for municipalities, almost 0.5bn CZK for regions and smaller sums for the state and the railways, with an effective date of July 2027.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions) for the draft surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDXBH65S3; the veklep id is not re-minted. The RIA's own problem statement is that sewer infrastructure carries stormwater from a surface whether or not that surface is exempt, so the cost is not borne by whoever creates the load; it also ties the change to directive 2024/3019, which treats urban runoff as a component of urban wastewater. Dates: authorised 2026-08-27, comment procedure open; effective 07/2027. Duty-holders newly billed: the state (Ministry of Transport, Ceske drahy, Sprava zeleznic), regions for class II and III roads, municipalities for local roads, and households in buildings on combined sewers. Market: impervious-area measurement and cadastral surface mapping, stormwater retention and infiltration retrofits that cut the billable area, and billing-side software for water companies that must now invoice surfaces they never invoiced.
quote: Jedná se o roční dopady ve výši téměř 5 mld. Kč na rozpočty obcí v souvislosti s odváděním srážkových vod z komunikací, dopady ve výši téměř 0,5 mld. na rozpočty krajů v souvislosti s úhradou srážkových vod ze silnic II. a III. třídy

title: Zákon o obcích novela — shared-agenda platform answers the most fragmented municipal map in the OECD
money_note: Interior ministry prices the new register of voluntary municipal associations at 3-5m CZK to build plus about 1.2m CZK a year to run; the 3m CZK lower bound converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR. The Digital and Information Agency states its cost for the register of local representatives only as lower tens of millions CZK plus about 10m CZK a year, which is not quantified further
summary: The interior ministry bill amending Act 128/2000 deepens the spolecenstvi obci as a shared-services platform, letting municipalities pool capacity for agendas small ones cannot run alone such as a joint municipal police, and adds state-budget support, a register of voluntary municipal associations and a public register of mayors and similar officeholders. Its RIA argues from the fact that Czechia has the smallest average municipality in the OECD, 6254 of them averaging 1710 inhabitants, with public-administration costs of 63.1bn CZK in 2022, and proposes an effective date of 1 January 2027.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions) for the draft surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-ALBSDRFEKCIO; the veklep id is not re-minted and this record cites the Zaverecna zprava RIA attachment instead of the material page. RIA figures: median municipality 442 inhabitants, 96 percent under 5000 and 76 percent under 1000 in 2021, average area 13 km2 against an OECD average of 234 km2, count risen from 4100 in 1990 to 6230 in 1994 to 6254 now; DEA efficiency analysis (TACR TL01000463) puts peak relative efficiency at 10000-50000 inhabitants, and spolecenstvi obci formed so far average 21700 inhabitants (median 17600), inside that band. RIA explicitly excludes municipal mergers from scope. Dates: authorised 2026-02-19, signed, government-approved package dated 2026-07-30; effective 01/2027; ex-post RIA after five years. Market: shared back-office and shared-agenda software for microregions, joint procurement, the two new state registers as govtech procurements. The RIA also re-opens the odmenovani rules for concurrent elected offices set by Act 57/2025.
quote: ČR má nejmenší průměrnou velikost obce mezi zeměmi Organizace pro hospodářskou spolupráci a rozvoj (OECD), v průměru 1 710 obyvatel na obec. To je výrazně pod průměrem OECD, který činí 10 250 obyvatel, a průměrem EU, který činí 5 960 obyvatel.

title: Veřejné opatrovnictví — small municipalities get to hand the guardianship agenda to a capable neighbour
money_note: RIA calls the change budget-neutral; the standing envelope it names is 430m CZK of performance payments to municipalities and 21m CZK to regions, which the bill does not change
summary: The justice ministry bill amending the civil code and related acts lets a municipality transfer the public-guardianship function to another municipality or to a spolecenstvi obci by public-law contract, and lets a court appoint a different suitable municipality where the resident one cannot perform the role or is in conflict of interest. The RIA reports that small type I municipalities perform 75 percent of the agenda and that up to 80 percent of them guard only one to three people, with a proposed effective date of 1 July 2027.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions) for the draft surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDTFC490H; the veklep id is not re-minted and this record cites the RIA attachment. RIA problem statement: the rules on which municipality a court may appoint are too rigid, there is no alternative when the appointed municipality lacks staff (in small ones the mayor performs it personally), and there is no remedy at all for conflict of interest between guardian and ward. A 2016 interior ministry survey found 50 percent of municipalities would welcome a public-law contract option; the ombudsman supports it. The Supreme Administrative Court settled the competence question on 26 November 2025 (Komp 3/2018-181) in favour of MPSV. The existing option of a municipality-founded legal person under section 471(3) of the civil code is described as almost unused, with no standards, no mandatory liability insurance and unclear liability, and the bill removes it. Dates: authorised 2026-04-27, government meeting 2026-08-17, attachments dated 2026-09-01; effective 1 July 2027. Market: shared guardianship offices at microregion scale, case-management and asset-accounting software for guardians, training under vyhlaska 413/2024.
quote: Sběr počtu opatrovanců v roce 2025 ukazuje, že opatrovnictví vykonávají většinově malé obce typu I. (75 % obcí vykonávajících agendu veřejného opatrovnictví).

title: Dětský certifikát — child-work vetting extract becomes mandatory across schools, sport and childcare
money_note: No cost figure is published for the register build or for the vetting burden on employers
summary: Act 270/2025 creates an evidence skutecnosti dulezitych pro praci s detmi inside the criminal records register and a special extract from it, the so-called detsky certifikat, whose provisions take effect on 1 January 2027. A record blocks work as a teacher, in institutional and protective-care facilities, as a paediatrician or health worker, in child social-legal protection and in social services where the contact with children is direct and regular, and a clean extract becomes a condition for the licensed trades covering sport and physical-education services, day care of children under three, psychological counselling and diagnostics, and massage, reconditioning and regeneration services.
notes: Checklist source 3 (e-Sbirka). Verified mechanically against the e-Sbirka linked-data endpoint: GET https://opendata.eselpoint.gov.cz/esel-esb/eli/cz/sb/2025/270 with Accept text/turtle returns citace-pravniho-aktu '270/2025 Sb.' and ma-posledni-zneni eli/cz/sb/2025/270/2027-01-01, alongside versions 2025-08-05, 2026-01-01 and 2026-07-01 — so the staged effectiveness is machine-checkable, not asserted. Entry duration: 100 years for offences carrying an upper limit of at least five years, 20 years for less serious ones, not shortenable; entry is near-automatic for sexual and violent offences against life and health and discretionary for other intentional offences; legal persons can be entered too; juveniles are entered only on a court decision. Distinct from reg-cz-psilocybin-2026, which records the cannabis and psilocybin limbs of the same act: different duty, different duty-holders, different date. NO QUOTE CAPTURED — the e-Sbirka act text is served by a JavaScript application and no verbatim payload was retrieved, so the key is omitted rather than filled from secondary commentary. A future pass owes the section numbers straight from the consolidated text. Related: the forms decree surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDTRGAQDS implements the request forms for this extract, also effective 1 January 2027. Market: vetting workflow for every school, sports club, camp, childcare provider and social-services employer, and the four affected trade licences.

title: Poplatky za rádiové kmitočty — fee rewrite unblocks 26 GHz, the 3.8-4.2 GHz band and indoor small cells
money_note: The explanatory report quantifies the change's own effect on state revenue at plus 150000 CZK a year, converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR; the fee base it sits on is 1193676425 CZK collected by the telecom office in 2025, and future growth from the newly priced bands is explicitly left unquantified
summary: The industry ministry draft amending government regulation 154/2005 replaces the 200 MHz minimum channel width for pricing the 24.25 to 27.5 GHz band with 50 MHz in multiples of 5 MHz, prices indoor small-cell networks in production halls, creates a fee basis for terrestrial mobile use of 3800 to 4200 MHz, and adds a coefficient for earth stations talking to non-geostationary satellite constellations. The explanatory report states that today's rule forces licensees to pay for a channel they do not use, and proposes an effective date of 1 January 2027.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions) for the draft surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDVEAJNTM; the veklep id is not re-minted and this record cites the duvodova zprava attachment. No Zaverecna zprava RIA is attached — the reasoning sits in the duvodova zprava, which is stated rather than assumed. Other limbs: a fixed one-twelfth fee for licences valid under one month (demonstrations and product shows currently fall between administrative-procedure deadlines), a minimum fee for experimental licences that today fall under the 100 CZK non-collection threshold, and the 700 MHz guard blocks reserved for the integrated rescue system moved into coefficient K1. Dates: authorised 2026-06-29, comment procedure closed; effective 1 January 2027. Market: private and industrial 5G in manufacturing halls, fixed wireless access in areas where a 200 MHz channel was never needed, and satellite ground-segment operators who gain a predictable fee. Regulator: CTU.
quote: Stávající znění nařízení vlády č. 154/2005 Sb. tak nutí držitele k vyšším platbám za kanál, jehož šířku v plném rozsahu nepotřebují, a tedy ani s ohledem na aktuální potřebu nebo počet zákazníků nevyužívají.

title: Limit nákladů zdravotních pojišťoven — permanent 0.52 point cut to insurers' own-running budget
money_note: Explanatory report: about 3bn CZK stays in the basic fund for 2027 and the change is permanent, converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR. The state transfer into public health insurance rises by about 21bn CZK year on year, which is a separate measure
summary: The finance ministry decree amending vyhlaska 418/2003 cuts the constant in the coefficient that caps what a health insurer may move from the basic fund to its own operating, social and asset funds from 3.08 to 2.56, lowering the cap by 0.52 percentage points for every insurer. The explanatory report says the change is permanent, leaves about 3bn CZK in the basic fund for health services in 2027 and is meant to press insurers on operating efficiency, with an effective date of 1 January 2027.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions) for the draft surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDVYGNA4F; the veklep id is not re-minted and this record cites the duvodova zprava attachment. No Zaverecna zprava RIA is attached; the quantification sits in the duvodova zprava with a per-insurer table for 2027. The decree preserves the long-standing inverse relation between insured headcount and the permitted percentage. Legal basis: section 7(2) of Act 551/1991 and section 16(5) of Act 280/1992, both empowering the finance ministry to set the cost limit. Dates: authorised 2026-07-14, comment procedure closed; effective 1 January 2027. Market: cost-to-serve automation at the seven Czech health insurers — claims adjudication, document handling, contact-centre deflection — because the cap falls while the volume of covered services rises. The separate 21bn CZK state transfer is the funding side and is not this decree.
quote: Další 3 mld. Kč budou zajištěny snížením maximálního limitu nákladů na činnost zdravotní pojišťovny.

title: Dorovnávací daně novela — Pillar 2 filing, deadlines and payment rules rebuilt for Czech taxpayers
money_note: RIA calls the revenue effect negligible because it touches a marginal number of taxpayers; no figure is published
summary: The finance ministry draft amending Act 416/2023 folds the running OECD administrative guidance on the global minimum tax into Czech law and reworks four procedural points the OECD and directive 2022/2523 leave to member states: the annual notification that another taxpayer has filed the information return becomes a change-only filing on a proper form, the 22-month tax-return deadline is shortened towards the 15-month information-return deadline, and payment rules are added for taxpayers that are wound up or become insolvent before their liability is knowable. The RIA proposes an effective date of July 2027.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions) for the draft surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDXCGU8JB; the veklep id is not re-minted and this record cites the Zaverecna zprava RIA attachment. The RIA carries four separate Definice problemu sections, one per measure. State's own reasoning on the liquidation case: without a substitute instrument there is nobody to collect from after a taxpayer is wound up with no legal successor, and a taxpayer often cannot know its liability at the moment of liquidation because the group return has not been filed. RIA also flags the Commission's DAC recast proposal as a reason it cannot fix a review date. Dates: reference MF-30237/2026/32-8, authorised 2026-08-27, in comment procedure; effective 07/2027. Duty-holders: taxpayers under sections 112 and 117 of Act 416/2023, that is Czech entities of groups above the 750m EUR revenue threshold. Market: Pillar 2 filing and data-collection tooling, and advisory for groups whose only Czech obligation is the notification.
quote: V současné chvíli je nutné podávat oznámení o splnění povinnosti podat informační přehled každý rok, i ve chvíli, kdy údaje v oznámení (vyjma zdaňovacího období) jsou totožné.

title: Směrnice 2024/1385 — doxing and cyberflashing become crimes and courts get content-removal orders
money_note: No compliance cost is published in the directive or in the Czech draft's submission documents
summary: Directive 2024/1385 on combating violence against women requires member states to bring the necessary law into force by 14 June 2027, criminalising non-consensual sharing of intimate material including deepfakes, cyberstalking, cyberharassment covering unsolicited intimate images and doxing, and gender-based incitement online. The Czech justice ministry put its transposing amendment to the criminal code and to Act 45/2013 on victims into inter-ministerial comment procedure on 31 August 2026, adding individualised victim-needs assessment by police and then probation officers and court orders to remove harmful online content.
notes: Checklist source 3 (EUR-Lex) crossed with checklist source 4: the Czech transposing draft is the one the scripted feed surfaced as veklep-ALBSDXDLCV5W, and that id is not re-minted; this record is the dated EU obligation the draft answers, cited to EUR-Lex rather than to the material page. Transposition deadline read verbatim from Article 49(1) of the Czech language text on EUR-Lex; entry into force is the twentieth day after publication (Article 50), the directive was signed 14 May 2024 and the non-regression clause references 13 June 2024. Offence articles: 3 female genital mutilation, 4 forced marriage, 5 non-consensual intimate material including deepfakes, 6 cyberstalking, 7 cyberharassment (cyberflashing, doxing, coordinated online attacks), 8 cyber incitement. Czech draft: authorised 2026-08-31, no Zaverecna zprava RIA attached, duvodova zprava only. Market: platform-side takedown workflow and evidence preservation for services with Czech users, victim-assessment tooling for police and Probacni a mediacni sluzba.
quote: Členské státy uvedou v účinnost právní a správní předpisy nezbytné pro dosažení souladu s touto směrnicí do 14. června 2027.

title: Uznávání odborné kvalifikace — first Czech route to assess non-EU qualifications, after a CJEU ruling
money_note: No cost figure is published; the draft carries no Zaverecna zprava RIA
summary: The education ministry draft amending Act 18/2004 creates a way to assess professional qualifications obtained outside the European Union, above all where they rest on completed higher education, because today nothing exists beyond nostrification of the diploma and that is often not enough to admit someone to a regulated profession. The explanatory report states that the Court of Justice found in C-75/22 Commission v Czech Republic that Czechia failed to implement parts of directive 2005/36, and proposes an effective date of 1 January 2028.
notes: Checklist source 4 (VeKLEP RIA problem definitions) for the draft surfaced by the scripted feed as veklep-KORNDXAMWBJD; the veklep id is not re-minted and this record cites the duvodova zprava attachment. The amendment is the first full revision of the act since 2004 and is meant to cure the breach of Article 3(1)(g) and (h) and Article 51(1) of directive 2005/36 found in C-75/22. Other limbs: activities connected with the exercise of public authority are put expressly outside scope so nobody applies for recognition as a judge or prosecutor; paper applications for the European Professional Card are abolished because the procedure is fully electronic; and assessment of qualifications by a public-law employer is removed as unused and as a source of inconsistent decisions. Effective date read verbatim from the article-by-article part: 'Ucinnost je navrhovana na 1. ledna 2028.' Dates: authorised 2026-08-25, in comment procedure; the government legislative plan schedules it to government by 12.2026 with effect 01.28, which matches. Market: qualification-assessment services and document handling for third-country hires into Czech regulated professions, a direct lever on the labour shortage.
quote: Soudní dvůr EU v rozsudku C-75/22 Komise v. Česká republika konstatoval, že Česká republika tím, že nepřijala opatření podle čl. 3 odst. 1 písm. g) a h), čl. 7 odst. 3 a čl. 51 odst. 1 směrnice 2005/36/ES, nesplnila povinnosti, které pro ni vyplývají z této směrnice.

title: CRR3 operational risk — business-indicator standards and FINREP mapping bite from 23 September 2026
money_note: No compliance cost is published in either act
summary: Commission Delegated Regulation 2026/1167 and Implementing Regulation 2026/1166, both published on 3 September 2026, fix how banks build the business indicator that drives the CRR3 operational-risk capital charge and map each of its components to a named FINREP reporting cell. They set out the interest, lease, dividend, services and financial components, a seven-type loss taxonomy, notification when the prudential-boundary approach is used, and adjustment of the indicator after mergers, acquisitions and disposals, entering into force twenty days after publication.
notes: Checklist source 3 (EUR-Lex), read from the Official Journal L-series daily issues for 1, 2 and 3 September 2026. Directly applicable in every member state, so no Czech transposition step and no national discretion; supervision is CNB for Czech institutions and the ECB for significant ones. Both acts supplement Regulation 575/2013 as amended by the CRR3 package. Duty-holders: every credit institution in the EU, including small ones, because the business indicator is the common input to the standardised operational-risk approach that replaced the earlier methods. Absence check not applicable — this is an EU instrument, not a market-gap claim. Market: FINREP-to-business-indicator reconciliation tooling, operational-loss data collection to the new taxonomy, and the hedging-relationship documentation and controls the delegated act requires. No corpus record covers CRR3 operational risk: grep of data/signals for 'operational risk' and 'business indicator' returns zero.
quote: The items included in the calculation of the business indicator, as listed in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1167 shall be mapped to the cells of the FINREP templates laid down in Annex I to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/3117

title: Koeficient minimální mzdy — 0.446 for 2027 and 0.458 for 2028 on the path to 47 percent
money_note: No aggregate wage-bill figure is published; press coverage puts the resulting 2027 monthly minimum near 24900 CZK against a projected average wage of 55795 CZK, but the binding number is the finance ministry projection and is not yet in the Sbirka
summary: The labour ministry proposes a minimum-wage coefficient of 0.446 for 2027 and 0.458 for 2028, that is roughly 44.6 and 45.8 percent of the average wage, on a statutory glide path to the 47 percent that social partners agreed and the labour code assumes, to be reached in 2029. The monthly minimum is the finance ministry projection of the average gross nominal wage multiplied by the coefficient, the projection for 2027 was due by 31 August 2026 and the resulting amount is published in the Sbirka, so the number binds every employer from 1 January 2027.
notes: Checklist sources 2 and 4. The scripted veklep feed already holds this draft as veklep-KORNDV4MNCNT (data/signals/regulation/2026-08-25.jsonl) but carries urgency 0 and no dates, no coefficients and no glide-path target; that id is deliberately not re-minted and this record is the dated substance behind it, cited to the MPSV press release of 18 June 2026 rather than to the odok material page. Legal basis: section 111(9) of Act 262/2006 (zakonik prace), which has the government set coefficients two years ahead. Legislative plan item MPSV-6, to government 06.2026, effective 09.2026, RIA required. Process still open at the date of this pass: inter-ministerial comment procedure started 18 June 2026, then tripartite, then government. Why it matters beyond low earners, in the minister's own framing: the minimum wage feeds pay across the whole economy, and it also moves the OBZP health-insurance payment and the thresholds keyed to it. Market: payroll reconfiguration every January, wage-band compression analysis, and the guaranteed-wage levels derived from it.
quote: Ministerstvo práce a sociálních věcí navrhuje pro rok 2027 koeficient pro výpočet minimální mzdy ve výši 0,446 a pro rok 2028 koeficient ve výši 0,458.

title: Programové prohlášení vlády — dated motorway and rail commitments through 2027 and 2029
money_note: The programme names no budget; funding runs through the State Transport Infrastructure Fund and EU programmes, and the programme itself makes the high-speed-rail sections conditional on that fund's capacity
summary: The government programme declaration of 5 January 2026 puts hard dates on the transport build-out: D3 across South Bohemia to the Austrian connection and the Prague ring widening to Cerny Most by 2027, the remaining ring section started by 2028 at the latest, and by 2029 D11 completed and joined to Poland, D6, D35 to Mohelnice, the Prague to Ruzyne airport to Kladno link, ETCS on the main corridors and 5G coverage of every rail corridor. It also commits to opening the liniovy zakon again to speed up transport construction and to safety upgrades at up to 400 level crossings.
notes: Checklist source 1 (Programove prohlaseni vlady and its semi-annual fulfilment evaluations). This is a political commitment with dates, not an enacted obligation, and is scored as such: urgency 2 because the nearest commitments fall in 2027, recurrence 1 because a programme is remade with each government. The first semi-annual evaluation was held on 9 July 2026 at Kramarova vila and the prime minister named migration law, energy prices and housing as delivered; no written evaluation document is published on vlada.gov.cz, only the press event and per-minister video summaries, so the transport commitments have no published fulfilment status to check them against. Corpus already holds ETCS as a tender stream (75 records match ETCS or zeleznic across the ledgers, including Sprava zeleznic corridor contracts and ARRIVA and CD retrofits), so this record is the dated political commitment behind that pipeline rather than another instance of it. Market: rail telecom (FRMCS and 5G along corridors), ETCS onboard retrofit for every operator on those corridors, and level-crossing safety systems.
quote: Do roku 2029 pokryjeme všechny železniční koridory internetem 5G.

title: Cenovy vymer 1/2026/OLZP — the split trade margin stops applying to purely hospital medicines
money_note: A price ruling sets margins and maximum prices rather than an allocation; no sum is attached and none is estimated.
summary: The Czech health ministry price ruling 1/2026/OLZP of 24 October 2025, published in ministry bulletin 18/2025 and effective from 1 January 2026, regulates prices of medicinal products and foods for special medical purposes, and stops applying the split trade margin to purely hospital medicinal products. Companion rulings 2/2026/OLZP set ATC groups with special price rules for availability, and 3/2026/OLZP covers medical devices and in vitro diagnostics.
notes: DATES: issued 24 October 2025, published on the ministry site 31 October 2025 in Věstník 18/2025, in force 1 January 2026; the price rulings are reissued annually, hence recurrence 3. WHY IT BELONGS TO THIS TOPIC: it changes the margin structure on the exact goods the 106 drug-object dynamic-purchasing notices buy, from the same date the section 40d central-tendering power switches on, so a Czech hospital's drug purchasing economics changed twice on 1 January 2026. VERBATIM NOT TAKEN FROM THE PRIMARY: the ministry page carries only a header and a link to Cenovy-vymer-c.-1_2026_OLZP.pdf, so no quote is recorded rather than a quote attributed to a page that does not contain it. The hospital-margin change is reported by havelpartners.blog/nove-cenove-vymery-ministerstva-zdravotnictvi-pro-rok-2026-co-se-meni-a-na-co-si-dat-pozor (6 January 2026) as 'dělená obchodní přirážka se nově neuplatní u čistě nemocničních léčivých přípravků', and by epravo.cz article 120661; a future pass owes a read of the PDF itself.
